title: The Technical Debt Feedback Loop
description: Explore the technical debt doom loop and three leverage-point interventions that break it.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Organizational Silos and Silo Busting

educational.learningObjective: Given the technical-debt reinforcing loop, the learner will identify which leverage-point intervention would most effectively break the cycle for a system already showing signs of being a legacy system.
prerequisites: Can read a causal loop diagram
learningOutcomes: Trace the technical debt reinforcing loop
Compare three candidate interventions by where they cut the loop
Justify an intervention choice for a system already showing legacy symptoms
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Give learners a described legacy system and ask which of the three interventions they would fund first, with a justification tied to where it cuts the loop.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Causal loop diagram with a toggled intervention overlay
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Intervention comparison against a fixed loop structure
pedagogical.feedbackType: Side-panel explanations for every node and intervention
misconceptionsAddressed: That technical debt is only a code quality problem
That the loop can be broken by working harder inside it
discussionQuestions: Why does 'we'll clean it up next sprint' almost never happen?
Is technical debt always bad, or is some of it a reasonable trade?
What is the organizational equivalent of technical debt?
